title: Kubernetes od nule
tagline: Od jednog poslužitelja do klastera koji se sam popravlja – na primjeru aplikacije za menzu.
runningExample: KLOPA: a fictional student-built app for pre-ordering lunch at a campus canteen (menza). Daily 12:00 lunch rush = natural recurring load spike; 'Ćevap-petak' = Friday flash crowd; 'ispitni rok' = week-long growth. Components (grow over the course): klopa-web (TypeScript frontend built with npm/Vite, served by nginx), klopa-api (Python/Django behind gunicorn with synchronous workers: one request per worker, ≈256 MB per worker – exactly the worker-pool server the M1 sims model, labelled as such; a DeepDive in L02 explains how Node.js/Go/async servers differ), klopa-worker (Python RabbitMQ consumer via pika: kitchen tickets, SMS 'narudžba je spremna'), Postgres, Redis (sessions/cache), RabbitMQ (orders queue), external SMS gateway. Fixed names: domain klopa.example (RFC 2606 reserved – never klopa.hr), registry registry.klopa.example, namespaces klopa and klopa-staging, app port 8000 (gunicorn), web 8080 (unprivileged nginx). Version chain (klopa-api tags): 1.3.2 (v1, blue) → 1.4.0 'vegetarijanski meni' (L13, v2 violet) → 1.5.0 broken (rose, L13) → 2.0.0 'nova košarica' with a VAT bug: rolled out with RollingUpdate in the L20 hook, rolled back; the L20 sim shows a canary stopping it → 2.0.1 VAT fix shipped through CI + Argo CD (L21–L22) → 2.0.2 hotfix for the Ćevap-petak discount (L24). Cast (fictional, gender-balanced, only in short story beats/speech bubbles – the only place colloquial verbs like 'deployati' are allowed): Lana (backend dev), Davor (ops/on-call; announces Erasmus in L20, is gone by L23 = bus factor), Petra (product, brings requirements), Iva (new teammate from L06/L07, fresh eyes and new mistakes), teta Mira (kitchen, voice of physical consequences: „Dvaput ćevapi?!”). Narrative devices: (1) incident card at the top of each lecture (day/time, symptom, req/s, p95, errors) – every number must be reproducible in that lecture's sim with the preset and seed printed on the card; (2) 'Cijena rješenja' box at the end = next lecture's incident (hook/bridge chain); (3) Klopa karta (src/kit/story/story-map.ts) grows each lecture: 01 users→DNS→laptop/VPS; 02 one VPS resized 2 vCPU/2 GB → 4 vCPU/8 GB + Postgres; 03 second server (srednji), shared DB; 04 load balancer, 3 servers (Mali 1/2, Srednji 2/4, Veliki 4/8); 05 health checks + Redis; 06 RabbitMQ + worker + SMS gateway; 07–09 containers on one Compose host; 10 cluster box; 11 control plane + 3 nodes; 12 Pod; 13 Deployment/ReplicaSet; 14 Service; 15 Gateway; 16 ConfigMap/Secret; 17 node sizes/requests; 18 HPA + Cluster Autoscaler + KEDA on worker; 19 Postgres StatefulSet + PVC (labelled 'u tečaju StatefulSet; u produkciji upravljana baza ili operator'); 20 staging/prod environments; 21 CI + registry; 22 config repo + Argo CD; 23 secret store + ESO; 24 complete + observability. (4) Optional 'Davorov dežurni priručnik' (symptom → cause → command) grows from L11 and is downloadable in L24. Six shared sim engines (pure TS, seeded): E1 Promet (LB/traffic), E2 Red (queue; Kafka only as a DeepDive stepper), E3 Klaster (controllers, scheduler, probes, rollout, HPA/CA), E4 Tvornica (build cache, pipeline), E5 Tko vidi? (secret access graph), E6 Git↔klaster (Argo CD).
styleGuide: Croatian rules for lecture authors (overrides earlier outlines; docs/AUTHORING.md must be aligned – see designRationale). ADDRESS: plural 'vi' (lowercase) for instructions/tasks ('Dodajte poslužitelj…'), inclusive 'mi' for walk-throughs ('Pošaljimo 100 zahtjeva…'); never 'ti'; avoid singular gendered forms. Sim recap label: „Što ste upravo vidjeli”. Buttons/controls: short singular imperative, no full stop ('Pošalji promet', 'Sruši proces'). Objectives are infinitive phrases completing the generated hero 'Nakon ovog predavanja moći ćete…'. STANDARD CROATIAN, IJEKAVICA: točka, tisuća, uvjet, promet (not saobraćaj), računalo, datoteka, operacijski sustav, sigurnost, tko/što, 'je li' (not 'da li'), sljedeći, postupno (not postepeno), postaviti/konfigurirati (not podesiti), trenutačno (currently), omogućuje, ako (not ukoliko), budući da. Use 'podatci' (IHJJ) site-wide. TERMS: poslužitelj in prose ('server' OK in sim UI labels); raspodijeljeni sustav (mention 'distribuirani' once in L03); load balancer (EN); raspodjela opterećenja; kontejner (never spremnik); slika kontejnera (engl. image) – short 'slika' once clear, 'image' only in code/kubectl output, figures are 'prikaz/dijagram/animacija'; pictures of food are 'fotografije' (never 'slike', which collides with container images); čvor (Node only for the API object); klaster; upravljačka ravnina (never 'master'); red poruka; željeno stanje; petlja usklađivanja; provjera živosti/spremnosti/pokretanja for Kubernetes probes; 'provjera ispravnosti' for every other health check (load balancer, Compose healthcheck) – one translation only; 'procesorska jezgra' for CPU cores, 'jezgra (operacijskog sustava)' for the kernel – never bare 'jezgra' where both could be meant; WORKER: in L02/L04/L05 'radnik (engl. worker)' = a server's worker process; in L06+ queue consumers are 'potrošači'; the word 'worker' stays only in the name klopa-worker; `requests`/`limits` in code font with gloss 'zajamčeni minimum / gornja granica' (never translate request as 'zahtjev' – collides with HTTP zahtjev). DEPLOY FAMILY: Deployment = the Kubernetes object (always capitalised); postavljanje (engl. deploy) = the act of getting a version running in an environment; izdanje = release; uvođenje = rollout; isporuka = software delivery in general; kontinuirana isporuka = continuous delivery; kontinuirano postavljanje = continuous deployment. GIT VERBS: in UI and prose say 'spremiti u Git' / 'commit' as a noun (commit/commita/commitovi); never 'commitati/commitaj' outside story speech bubbles. DECLENSION: Kubernetes kinds in PascalCase with endings, no hyphen: Pod/Poda/Podovi/Podova, Deployment/Deploymenta/Deploymenata, Service/Servicea/Serviceu (avoid plural: 'objekti Service'), Secret/Secreta, ConfigMap/ConfigMapa, ReplicaSet/ReplicaSeta, Namespace/Namespacea, Gateway/Gatewaya/Gatewayem, Dockerfile/Dockerfilea, pipeline/pipelinea. Abbreviations with hyphen: RAM-a, CPU-a, API-ja, YAML-a, HPA-a, Argo CD-a. Never decline code: 'naredbom `kubectl apply`', 'agent `kubelet`', 'baza `etcd`'. CODE FONT EVERYWHERE: commands, file names, fields, tags and addresses in hooks, bridges, subtitles and incident cards are written in backticks (`localhost:8000`, `.env`, `latest`, `kubectl apply`, `replicas: 3`, `secret.yaml`); hero and incident card render inline code. First use: hrvatski termin (engl. *term*). TYPOGRAPHY: „…” quotes; decimal comma (0,6 s); space before % and units (50 %, 2 GB); en dash ranges (2–4); sentence-case headings; dates '1. listopada 2026.'; plural counters via Intl.PluralRules('hr'). AVOID MT SMELLS: 'od strane', 'vršiti', 'isti' as pronoun, 'koristeći X', 'na dnevnoj bazi', 'baziran na', 'što da radi', Title Case. FACTS: version numbers only in code blocks or fact callouts with '(stanje: listopad 2026.)'; story text never names a software version. INCIDENT NUMBERS: every number on an incident card or in a hook must be reproducible in that lecture's sim with a stated preset and seed (store the seed on the card); sim cards state the run length. MISCONCEPTIONS: given as a Croatian myth sentence plus an English correction; use the Croatian sentence in MythOrFact and the correction as the explanation. ANALOGIES: always with 'breaks down'. AVOIDED ANALOGIES (never render as Analogy): 'prometni policajac' for a load balancer (L04 – suggests the LB sees the whole road); 'dirigent' for Kubernetes (L10 – shown only as a myth: a conductor runs a script and the music stops with him); 'sef' or 'zapečaćena omotnica' for a Secret (L16 – implies encryption). Tone: friendly, concrete, short sentences, real Klopa numbers, no hype.

scenes.title: Zašto Petra ne vidi localhost
scenes.concept: Loopback 127.0.0.1 always means 'this machine'.
scenes.visual: Packet leaves Petra's phone addressed to localhost and U-turns back into her own phone with the label „127.0.0.1 = ovo računalo”.

scenes.title: Put zahtjeva korak po korak
scenes.concept: DNS (resolver, TTL cache; a missing name costs one resolver round trip and returns NXDOMAIN) → IP → TCP handshake (1 RTT) → TLS 1.3 (1 RTT) → HTTP request/response → process listening on a port; status families 2xx/4xx/5xx; 502/503/504 named for later.
scenes.visual: Stepper; packet header label (src IP:port → dst IP:port) rewrites at each hop; a waterfall bar grows.

scenes.title: Tko sluša na kojim vratima
scenes.concept: A process binds IP:port. 127.0.0.1 = only this machine; 0.0.0.0 or :: = all interfaces. Defaults differ: gunicorn and Django runserver bind 127.0.0.1:8000, Node's server.listen(port) binds all interfaces. By default one process per IP:port (SO_REUSEPORT and gunicorn's/Node's pre-fork master sharing one socket are deliberate exceptions). Even bound to 0.0.0.0, a laptop on home or campus Wi-Fi has a private address (192.168.x.x, 10.x) behind NAT, so Petra on mobile data still cannot reach it – that is why we rent a server with a public IP. Firewall in front of the doors.
scenes.visual: Building (IP) with doors (ports); toggle bind address and watch an external packet bounce or enter; second process on same port shows 'address already in use'; a second view puts the building behind a NAT router labelled „privatna adresa”.

scenes.title: Udaljenost je latencija
scenes.concept: Light in fibre ≈200 000 km/s → ≥1 ms RTT per 100 km; Zagreb→Frankfurt ≥7,2 ms, →Sydney ≥160 ms; new HTTPS connection ≥3 RTT before first byte.
scenes.visual: Map with server-location dropdown and animated round-trip counter labelled 'donja granica'.

scenes.title: Prvo postavljanje: s laptopa na poslužitelj
scenes.concept: Informal deploy (postavljanje): rent a VPS with 2 vCPU/2 GB and a public IP, copy code, run gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:8000, add a DNS A record; Petra opens http://klopa.example:8000. One line: in practice a reverse proxy (Caddy/nginx) listens on :443, terminates TLS and forwards to the app – the app may then listen on 127.0.0.1, which is safer (DeepDive). Chip: postavljanje ≠ Kubernetesov Deployment (L13).
scenes.visual: Code travels laptop → VPS; DNS record appears; Petra's request reaches the VPS; optional proxy box slides in front; Klopa karta v1.

flagshipSimulation.name: Put jednog zahtjeva
flagshipSimulation.description: Packet tracer: pick a scenario, the request walks resolver → DNS → TCP → TLS → HTTP → app while a waterfall builds; break-it toggles produce distinct symptoms. Zadaci: „Dijagnosticirajte četiri pokvarena URL-a samo po simptomu”, „Dovedite Petrin zahtjev do odgovora 200”.
controls: Odabir scenarija: Lanin laptop / VPS bez proxyja (http, :8000) / VPS s proxyjem (https, :443)
Prekidač „Zapis pokazuje na staru IP adresu”
Izbornik „Lokacija poslužitelja”: Zagreb / Frankfurt / Ashburn / Sydney
flagshipSimulation.model: Deterministic step model. DNS: NXDOMAIN → answer after one resolver RTT, stop – no TCP connection is ever attempted; stale A record → TCP to an IP where nothing answers → client timeout (or, variant, a different server answers 404). Scenario 'Lanin laptop': external client → private IP behind NAT → unroutable → timeout, labelled 'privatna adresa iza NAT-a', whatever the bind address. TCP to IP:port: firewall DROP (cloud security groups, ufw default) → no reply, client waits full client timeout (5 s sim) → hollow 'timeout' glyph; tooltip: a REJECT rule would answer at once and look like 'refused'. Nothing listening OR app bound to 127.0.0.1 with an external client (no-proxy scenario) → RST within 1 RTT → spiky 'connection refused' glyph (same request from the server itself succeeds). With-proxy scenario: the proxy on the same host reaches an app on 127.0.0.1 fine (DeepDive), 'Aplikacija ne radi' → proxy answers 502. Then TLS 1.3 1 RTT (https only), HTTP 1 RTT → 200. RTT lower bound = great-circle km / 100 ms (Split 2,6; Frankfurt 7,2; Ashburn 72,5; Sydney 160 ms), always labelled 'donja granica, stvarna je veća'. TTFB on a new HTTPS connection = DNS (0 if cached) + 3·RTT + server 20 ms (http: 2·RTT). Refused and timeout must never share timing.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: NXDOMAIN stops before any TCP connection; a DROP firewall or a stale DNS record hangs until timeout (hollow); app down or bound to 127.0.0.1 gives instant 'connection refused' (spiky); the laptop scenario times out whatever the bind address; a Sydney server stretches the waterfall to ≥480 ms before the first byte.
flagshipSimulation.insight: Every symptom points to a layer – name, address, door, process; 'refused' and 'timeout' tell different stories, and distance costs time no code can remove.

misconceptions: „localhost je moj poslužitelj” — 127.0.0.1 always means the machine making the request.
„Domena pokazuje na moju aplikaciju” — DNS returns only an IP; the port is separate (80/443 by default).
„Connection refused znači da je poslužitelj spor” — refused = nothing listens (fast); silently dropped or unreachable = timeout.
„Ako slušam na 0.0.0.0, svi me mogu dohvatiti” — a laptop behind NAT has a private address; you need a public IP (and an open firewall).
„Latencija se može optimizirati do nule” — the speed of light sets a floor.
keyFacts: [sim-models] Minimum RTT ≈1 ms per 100 km of fibre (light ≈200 000 km/s); Zagreb→Split ≥2,6 ms, Frankfurt ≥7,2 ms, Ashburn ≥72,5 ms, Sydney ≥160 ms (lower bounds).
[sim-models] New HTTPS connection: TCP 1 RTT + TLS 1.3 1 RTT (TLS 1.2: 2) + HTTP 1 RTT ⇒ ≥3 RTT to first byte; QUIC merges transport and crypto into 1 RTT.
[tech-facts] gunicorn and Django runserver bind 127.0.0.1:8000 by default; Node's server.listen(port) without a host binds :: / 0.0.0.0.
[tech-facts] Private ranges 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 are not routable on the internet (NAT).
Use the reserved domain klopa.example in all examples (never a real domain).
analogies: DNS = imenik (ime → broj). Breaks down: the phone book doesn't know whether anyone answers or on which port.
IP + port = zgrada i vrata stana. Breaks down: a port is not a security boundary, and by default exactly one process lives behind one IP:port (SO_REUSEPORT is a deliberate exception).
Privatna adresa = kućni broj sobe u studentskom domu. Breaks down: NAT lets you call out but nobody outside can dial your room directly.

scenes.title: Što poslužitelj radi sa zahtjevom
scenes.concept: Worker-pool server: each in-flight request holds a radnik (engl. worker) process (RAM) and needs CPU time; while waiting on the DB it holds RAM but no CPU; W = floor((RAM−512 MB)/256 MB). Visible Callout „Model”: Klopin API je Django iza gunicorna sa sinkronim radnicima – jedan radnik obrađuje jedan zahtjev i zauzima ≈256 MB (kao PHP-FPM ili Puma). DeepDive „A Node.js, Go, async Python?”: one process serves many requests concurrently with async I/O; JavaScript runs on one core per process (scale with a process per core or more Pods), and concurrency is usually capped by the DB connection pool.
scenes.visual: Server glyph with vCPU lanes, RAM worker slots and a small queue; one request's life as a shrinking CPU clock, then I/O wait.

scenes.title: Prosjek laže
scenes.concept: Nearest-rank percentiles over successful requests only; the mean hides the tail.
scenes.visual: Latency histogram with a draggable tail; mean barely moves while p99 explodes.

scenes.title: Hokejaška palica
scenes.concept: Labelled 'model M/M/1 (jedan poslužitelj, slučajni dolasci i trajanja)': W/S = 1/(1−ρ) – 2× at 0,5, 3,3× at 0,7, 5× at 0,8, 10× at 0,9, 100× at 0,99; caused by randomness. With c parallel workers the knee moves right (Erlang C, c=4 at ρ=0,95 → ≈5,5×, not 20×) but is still there. Little's law in a DeepDive.
scenes.visual: Utilisation slider drives the curve with a „vi ste ovdje” dot; predict the shape first; toggle c = 1 / 4.

scenes.title: Jezgre ili RAM?
scenes.concept: Validated: 2 vCPU, API preset ≈10 rps at 2/4/8 GB; I/O preset 2 GB ≈5,7 rps at ~15 % CPU, 4 GB ≈13, 8 GB ≈27.
scenes.visual: Same server, two workload tabs, RAM selector, goodput bar.

scenes.visual: Catalogue cards 1→8 vCPU, 2→16 GB with €/mj.; resize animation with a grey downtime band.

flagshipSimulation.name: Jedan poslužitelj protiv ručka
flagshipSimulation.description: E1 with one worker-pool server under Poisson traffic. Zadaci: „Preživite 12:00 uz p95 < 1 s i < 1 % grešaka na najjeftinijem poslužitelju”, „Pronađite opterećenje za koje više RAM-a ne pomaže”. Incident card preset: I/O, 2 vCPU/2 GB, λ 4 → nalet ×3, seed 42.
controls: Segmented opterećenje: API / I/O (čeka bazu) / CPU (obrada fotografija)
flagshipSimulation.model: sim-models SIM 1, single server. DT 10 ms, seeded mulberry32, Poisson arrivals (default λ 10, burst ×3 for 30 s). Presets (cpuMs exponential mean / ioMs fixed / memMB): API 200/300/256, I/O 50/1000/256, CPU 400/50/256. BASE_RAM 512 MB; W = max(1, floor((RAM−512)/memMB)) → 1 GB:2, 2:6, 4:14, 8:30, 16:62. Admit if inflight<W, else queue (QUEUE_MAX 10), else 503. Per tick share = min(1, vCPU/nCpu) (one request never uses >1 core); cpu then io; queued age > 5000 ms → 504; completed after timeout → 504 'wasted work'. No proxy yet: crash = connection refused (counted as 'odbijeno'). Unbounded workers: BASE + inflight·mem > RAM → OOM crash, restart after 6 s. Resize: down 20 s sim (badge 'stvarno: minute'). Metrics: goodput 5 s window; errors 10 s split 503/504/odbijeno; p50/p95/p99 nearest-rank over last 10 s successes, 'n/a' if n<20; CPU%, busy/W, RAM. Validated: API preset ≈10 rps regardless of RAM; I/O preset 2 GB ≈5,7 rps at ~15 % CPU, 4 GB ≈13, 8 GB ≈27 (λ 30); unbounded on 1 vCPU/2 GB at λ 4 → ~11 OOM crashes in 120 s, goodput ~0,8 vs ~4 rps bounded. Hook numbers (prototype lb-sim, I/O preset, 2 vCPU/2 GB, seed 42): λ 4 → p95 ≈1,5 s, 0 % errors, CPU ≈12 %; λ 12 → goodput 5,6–5,7 rps, p95 ≈3,0 s, ≈53 % errors – all 503 (queue full), CPU ≈15–16 %. With QUEUE_MAX 10 overload yields 503s; 504s appear only with a longer queue (Napredno 30 → bufferbloat, goodput collapses). Cost linear per vCPU, labelled 'ilustrativno'.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: „Izvuci utikač” takes availability to zero; „Neograničeni radnici” turns 2 GB into an OOM crash loop; every resize shows a downtime gap and the catalogue ends with „Nema većeg”; a 30-slot queue turns 503s into 504s and wasted work.
flagshipSimulation.insight: A server can be full while its CPU idles, because RAM bounds how many workers fit; more RAM does nothing for a CPU-bound app; latency explodes near 100 %; one machine is always a single point of failure.

misconceptions: „Više RAM-a = brži poslužitelj” — for this app server RAM bounds concurrency and cores bound throughput; for a database RAM is cache (page cache, shared_buffers) and does speed up reads (L05, L19).
„Latencija raste linearno s opterećenjem” — it grows like 1/(1−ρ) in M/M/1; more workers move the knee, they don't remove it.
„Prosječna latencija je dovoljna” — watch p95/p99; the mean hides the tail.
„Vertikalno skaliranje je zastarjelo” — often the right first move; its limits are the ceiling, the restart gap and the SPOF.
„70 % CPU-a znači 30 % rezerve” — in M/M/1 at 70 % the wait is already 3,3× the service time; more cores move the knee, they don't remove it.
keyFacts: [sim-models] Validated single-server numbers listed in the model (incl. hook preset and seed).
[sim-models] In the cloud price per vCPU is roughly linear within an instance family – do not draw an exponential cost curve.

scenes.title: Tri razloga
scenes.concept: Capacity beyond the biggest machine, availability beyond one machine, proximity to users; scale up vs scale out; replication (same app ×N) vs decomposition (microservices). Term raspodijeljeni (also distribuirani) sustav.
scenes.visual: One tall server morphs into many short ones; three reason cards.

scenes.title: Trebate li ovo uopće?
scenes.concept: Many apps run fine on one server; distribute only when load, availability or geography require it.
scenes.visual: Checklist producing a verdict.

scenes.title: Matematika devetki
scenes.concept: A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) (moved here from L02); series ΠAᵢ (2×99 % → 98,01 %); parallel 1−Π(1−Aᵢ) (2×99 % → 99,99 %); LB 99,99 % × app pair × single DB 99,9 % ≈ 99,88 %; 10 servers at 99 % → at least one down ≈9,6 % of the time.
scenes.visual: Scrubbable numbers inside formulas; small multiples for 1/2/3 replicas.

scenes.title: Zašto 10 × poslužitelja ≠ 10 × propusnosti
scenes.concept: Shared bottleneck (DB); Amdahl p=0,95 → max 20× (model). USL α=0,05, β=0,001 → peak N≈31 then decline – in a closed DeepDive, labelled as a model.
scenes.visual: Add app servers until the DB bar saturates; Amdahl curve; USL curve with scrubbable α, β inside the DeepDive.

scenes.title: Spor ili mrtav?
scenes.concept: Partial failure and the fallacies (lost, delayed, duplicated, reordered, partitioned); a slow node looks like a dead one; timeouts trade false alarms against waiting.
scenes.visual: Mini-game: pick a timeout against hidden faults (crash, GC pause, packet loss) and see false alarms vs user wait; six flip cards.

scenes.title: Dodajmo drugi poslužitelj
scenes.concept: Cliffhanger: DNS still points to server 1, so server 2 idles.
scenes.visual: Two servers, all dots to server 1, server 2 at 0 %.

flagshipSimulation.name: Arhitekt dostupnosti
flagshipSimulation.description: Build Klopa as a chain (ulaz → poslužitelji aplikacije × N → baza), set availability, failure domain and capacity per component, then run a seeded 'godina u 10 sekundi'. Zadaci: „Dosegnite 99,9 % unutar budžeta”, „Pokažite da jedna baza od 99,9 % određuje cijeli lanac”, „Preživite kvar ormara”.
controls: Gumbi za kvar: „Kvar ormara”, „Loša konfiguracija na svim poslužiteljima”
flagshipSimulation.model: Analytic: A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR); series ΠAᵢ; parallel (need ≥1 of n) 1−Π(1−Aᵢ). Monte Carlo: 8760 hourly steps rendered in 10 s, seeded; each component fails with MTTR 4 h and MTBF = MTTR·A/(1−A); 'isti ormar' adds a shared rack failure process taking down all members at once. N+1 rule: app tier counts as down during lunch hours (12–14 h weekdays) if surviving capacity < peak load. Each failure adds 'detection time' of downtime. 'Loša konfiguracija' fails all app servers for 1 h. Outputs: downtime h/yr next to the formula, lost lunches, €/mj. (linear, illustrative). Defaults: 2 app servers 99 %, each able to carry 70 % of peak, DB 99,9 %, entry 99,99 % → ≈99,88 %, and one failure overloads the survivor (100/70 ≈ 143 %).
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: With the rack toggle on, „Kvar ormara” takes both app servers down together; „Loša konfiguracija” shows redundancy does not help against the same mistake everywhere; at 70 % of peak per server, losing one server overloads the other (≈143 %).
flagshipSimulation.insight: Redundancy pays only when failures are independent and survivors have spare capacity; the single database dominates the chain; more machines also means more things that fail.

misconceptions: „Dvostruko poslužitelja = dvostruki kapacitet” — a shared component (the DB) caps throughput.
„Raspodijeljeno je automatski pouzdanije” — more parts, more failures; reliability needs redundancy plus design.
„Mreža je pouzdana i brza” — messages get lost, delayed, duplicated and reordered.
„Dva poslužitelja od 99 % uvijek daju 99,99 %” — only with independent failures, failover and N+1 capacity.
„Svaka aplikacija treba mikroservise i Kubernetes” — many apps run fine on one server; distribute only when load, availability or geography demand it.
keyFacts: [math] A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR). Two 99 % in series = 98,01 %; in parallel = 99,99 %; LB 99,99 % × app pair × DB 99,9 % ≈ 99,88 %.
[sim-models] USL defaults α 0,05, β 0,001 → peak ≈31 nodes; Amdahl p 0,95 → max 20×; both labelled as models.
analogies: Tim kolega koji komuniciraju samo porukama. Breaks down: people can phone and use intuition; machines only have timeouts.
Više kuhara, jedan štednjak: more cooks don't help when the shared stove (DB) is the bottleneck. Breaks down: a DB can be replicated, a stove cannot be copied by software.
lectures.bridgeToNext: Drugi poslužitelj stoji i čeka jer DNS sve šalje na prvi. Davor u međuvremenu doda i treći: uz veliki (4 vCPU, 8 GB) Klopa sada ima mali (1 vCPU, 2 GB) i srednji (2 vCPU, 4 GB) poslužitelj. Netko mora dijeliti promet – i to pametno.

lectures.title: Load balancer: tko dijeli promet
lectures.subtitle: Algoritmi raspodjele na različito jakim poslužiteljima – i zašto pošteno ne znači jednako.
lectures.hook: Klopa ima tri poslužitelja: mali (1 vCPU, 2 GB), srednji (2 vCPU, 4 GB) i veliki (4 vCPU, 8 GB). Davor je najprije sve tri adrese stavio u DNS, ali DNS korisnike dijeli otprilike jednako – ne zna da je veliki poslužitelj četiri puta jači od malog, a kad jedan padne, klijenti njegovu adresu još minutama pamte. Zato postavlja load balancer s kružnim raspoređivanjem – i u 12:00 mali poslužitelj vraća greške dok veliki radi na četvrtini snage. Kako dijeliti promet pošteno?
objectives: objasniti što radi load balancer i zašto omogućuje horizontalno skaliranje
konfigurirati poslužitelje s različitim brojem procesorskih jezgri i količinom RAM-a te predvidjeti njihov kapacitet
usporediti kružno i težinsko raspoređivanje te algoritam najmanje aktivnih veza na istom prometu
objasniti zašto se razlika među algoritmima vidi u p95, p99 i greškama, a ne u prosjeku
razlikovati L4 (veze) i L7 (zahtjevi) raspodjelu opterećenja

scenes.title: DNS kao load balancer?
scenes.concept: Played as the hook animation. Several A records: resolvers rotate the order, so clients spread roughly evenly by count. DNS cannot weight 1:2:4, does not know which server is alive, and caches (resolver, OS, browser, sometimes ignoring TTL) keep a dead IP in use; a whole campus behind one caching resolver shares one answer per TTL, so the split is lumpy.
scenes.visual: Three A records rotating; even split despite unequal servers; a dead server still receiving cached clients; TTL countdown.

scenes.title: Vi ste load balancer
scenes.concept: Manual mode: the student routes each request by clicking a server, gets overwhelmed, then presses „Automatski”.
scenes.visual: Request queue at the LB with click targets; arrival rate rises.

scenes.title: Koliko može koji poslužitelj?
scenes.concept: cap_cpu = vCPU·1000/cpuMs; W = floor((RAM−512)/memMB) radnika; cap_mem = W·1000/(cpuMs+ioMs); capacity ≈ min. API preset: Mali 5, Srednji 10, Veliki 20 req/s; 4 vCPU/2 GB is RAM-bound at 12; I/O preset 4/2 → 5,7 vs 1/8 → 20.
scenes.visual: Server builder card with sliders and live capacity.

scenes.title: Predvidite: 4 GB ili 8 GB?
scenes.concept: Predict before the flagship (the lecturer's 2/4 GB example): „Srednji poslužitelj (2 vCPU, 4 GB) i poslužitelj s 2 vCPU i 8 GB – koji obradi više API zahtjeva?” Correct: „Jednako, oko 10 u sekundi.” Explain: procesorske jezgre određuju propusnost; RAM pomaže tek kad zahtjevi dugo čekaju bazu – prebacite opterećenje na I/O. Leads directly into the flagship's second task.
scenes.visual: Predict card with two server cards; reveal runs both on the same seed.

scenes.title: Ljestve algoritama
scenes.concept: Main path: Nasumično, Kružno (round robin), Težinsko kružno (smooth WRR), Najmanje veza (inflight+queued; weighted (active+1)/w) – one-sentence rule each. Under Napredno + DeepDive: Dva nasumična izbora (power of two choices), Najkraće vrijeme odgovora.
scenes.visual: Same 12 requests routed by each algorithm side by side.

scenes.title: Kad se poslužitelj uspori
scenes.concept: „Spori disk” (CPU work ×3): static weights keep feeding it, least connections adapts; weights fit only one workload mix.
scenes.visual: One server turns amber; per-server queue bars.

scenes.title: Omotnica: L4 ili L7
scenes.concept: L4 sees IP:port and balances connections (NLB, Kubernetes Service); L7 reads host/path/cookie, balances requests, routes /api vs /fotografije, retries, terminates TLS; keep-alive over L4 pins a client (pays off in L14; L7 algorithms return at the Gateway in L15).
scenes.visual: Envelope metaphor with toggle; a keep-alive client stream sticks to one server.

flagshipSimulation.name: Load balancer u vašim rukama
flagshipSimulation.description: The lecturer's sim (E1): build a rack of heterogeneous servers, pick an algorithm and traffic, watch per-server CPU lanes, RAM radnik slots and queues, p50/p95/p99 and errors split 502/503/504; same seed for fair comparisons; small multiples of three algorithms. Zadaci: „0 % grešaka pri λ = 20 sa zadanim poslužiteljima”, „Pokažite da 2 vCPU/4 GB i 2 vCPU/8 GB jednako vrijede za API, zatim pronađite opterećenje u kojem 8 GB pobjeđuje”, „Najjeftiniji skup koji pri λ = 25 drži p95 < 1,5 s”. Incident card: λ 15, Kružno, API preset, seed 42.
controls: Slagač: Mali (1 vCPU/2 GB), Srednji (2/4), Veliki (4/8) ili Prilagođeni (vCPU 1–8, RAM 1–16 GB)
Segmented algoritam: Ručno, Nasumično, Kružno (round robin), Težinsko kružno (uredive težine), Najmanje veza, Težinski najmanje veza; Napredno: Dva nasumična izbora, Najkraće vrijeme odgovora
Klizač „Promet” 1–50 zahtjeva/s; uzorak stalni / valovi / nalet
Segmented opterećenje: API / I/O / CPU (obrada fotografija)
Gumb „Ponovi isti promet” i prikaz „Usporedi tri algoritma”
Gumbi za kvar: „Spori disk”, „Nalet u 12:00”, „Neograničeni radnici”
flagshipSimulation.model: sim-models SIM 1 exactly. DT 10 ms; BASE 512 MB; QUEUE_MAX 10; client timeout 5000 ms; λ default 10; defaults S1 1/2 GB, S2 2/4, S3 4/8; presets API 200/300/256, I/O 50/1000/256, CPU 400/50/256. Route among healthy servers: inflight<W → start, else queue<QUEUE_MAX → enqueue, else 503. share = min(1, vCPU/nCpu); queued age > timeout → 504; late completion → 504. Smooth WRR: cw[i]+=w[i], pick max, cw[pick]−=Σw; weights ∝ capacity (1:2:4). LC and least-response use active = inflight+queued; least response = EWMA(α 0,2)·(active+1); P2C = two distinct random healthy, fewer active. 'Spori disk' ×3 CPU demand. Unbounded workers → OOM: inflight+queued → 502, restart 6 s. Percentiles over successes only. Validated (seed 42, 300 s): λ15 RR 2,7 % errors p95 3,2 s (S1 98 % CPU, S3 27 %), WRR 0 %/1,0 s, LC 0 %/1,2 s; λ20 RR 10,6 %, WRR 0 %, LC 0,1 %; λ30 RR 18,9 %, WRR 0,2 %, LC 0,6 %, P2C 1,5 %, LRT 0,1 %; λ35 (=capacity) RR 25,9 %, WRR 4 %, LC 4,6 %, P2C 8,7 %. Random ≈ RR. Mixed I/O (4/2 GB vs 1/8 GB) λ15: LC 0,4 % vs RR 11,8 %. Advanced: queue 30 + I/O on 2 GB → goodput collapses (bufferbloat); at API overload an 8 GB server can show more timeouts than 2 GB (more concurrency, same CPU). A disabled toggle „Kubernetes Service (L14)” is planted.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: „Spori disk” on the big server: WRR keeps sending it 4/7 of traffic and its queue overflows, least connections shifts load away; „Nalet u 12:00” pushes RR past the small server; „Neograničeni radnici” makes a 2 GB server OOM-crash in a loop (502).
flagshipSimulation.insight: Round robin doesn't know servers differ; procesorske jezgre set throughput, RAM sets concurrency; a better algorithm shows in p95/p99 and errors, not the average; a load balancer adds capacity, not speed.

codeArtifacts.title: nginx upstream: weight, least_conn, random two
codeArtifacts.purpose: Algorithms from the sim as real config (upstream servers on :8000)

misconceptions: „Round robin je pošten” — it ignores server size and request weight.
„Load balancer ubrzava svaki zahtjev” — it adds capacity and one hop, not speed.
„Više RAM-a = veća propusnost” — RAM bounds concurrency, cores bound throughput (2/4 GB and 2/8 GB give the same ~10 rps on the API preset).
„Promet se uvijek raspoređuje po zahtjevu” — L4 balancers balance connections; a keep-alive client sticks to one server.
„Najmanje veza je uvijek najbolje” — a fast-failing server looks least busy (black hole, L05).
keyFacts: [tech-facts] Classic LBs offer round robin, weighted RR, least connections…; IPVS documents rr, wrr, lc, wlc, lblc.

[tech-facts] A Kubernetes Service (kube-proxy in the default iptables/nftables mode) uses none of these algorithms: it picks a ready endpoint at random for each new connection, with no weights and no notion of node size; it does skip Pods that fail readiness (payoff in L12, L14).

[sim-models] NGINX default is weighted RR (also least_conn, ip_hash, hash consistent, random two least_conn); Envoy LEAST_REQUEST = power of two choices; AWS ALB: round robin default, least outstanding requests, weighted random.
analogies: Domaćin u restoranu raspoređuje goste za stolove za dvoje i za osmero. Breaks down: the host sees how busy each waiter is; an LB only knows connection counts and health checks, not how heavy a request is.
lectures.bridgeToNext: S težinskim raspoređivanjem ručak je preživio. Ali u 12:03 procesu na velikom poslužitelju ponestane memorije i sruši se, a load balancer mu još nekoliko sekundi šalje narudžbe. Usto, studenti se žale: „Košarica mi se sama ispraznila!”

lectures.subtitle: Kvar se nikad ne otkrije odmah, a košarica u memoriji poslužitelja nestaje s njim.

Nakon pokusa sa „sporim diskom” Davor je prešao na algoritam najmanje aktivnih veza – i propalo je 37 narudžbi prije nego što je load balancer shvatio što se dogodilo. scenes.title: Prozor otkrivanja
scenes.concept: Active check: unhealthy after U consecutive failures → detection between (U−1)·interval and U·interval (+timeout if hung). AWS ALB defaults 30 s / 5 s / healthy 5 / unhealthy 2 → detection ≈30–60 s after a crash, up to ≈65 s for a hung target; back in rotation only after 5 passing checks (≈150 s).
scenes.visual: Timeline with probe ticks and a red window of failed requests; badge „2 s (sim) · stvarno: 30 s (AWS ALB)”.

scenes.title: Pad, gašenje, zastoj ili pražnjenje
scenes.concept: Process crash → port closed → RST → instant 502; machine off → no RST, the LB waits for its connect timeout → 502/504, like a hang; hang → requests wait until timeout → 504 (hollow); drain → no new requests, in-flight finish. Callback to L01 refused vs timeout.
scenes.visual: Four servers react side by side to the same traffic.

scenes.title: Crna rupa
scenes.concept: Least connections + fast-failing server attracts traffic; crash the S3 process at λ 15: RR 11 vs LC 37 failures; passive ejection and LB retry fix it; N+1: survivors at 100 % of capacity.
scenes.visual: Dead server with 0 active pulling dots; capacity bars overflowing.

scenes.title: Gdje živi košarica
scenes.concept: In-memory session → next request elsewhere = „sesija izgubljena”; sticky cookie → uneven load, lost on crash, no rebalance on scale-out; Redis (Django SESSION_ENGINE with the Redis cache) → stateless app servers. (Kubernetes' IP-based affinity comes in L14.)
scenes.visual: 20 users with cart stacks drawn wherever state lives.

scenes.title: Kamera prelazi na bazu
scenes.concept: State moved to the DB → DB is the new bottleneck and SPOF; cache-aside: h 0,9, cache 1 ms, DB 20 ms → avg 3 ms, 10 % DB load. Closed DeepDive: read replicas scale reads not writes; async lag breaks read-your-writes; CAP applies only during a partition.
scenes.visual: Pan to DB; hit-ratio slider; in the DeepDive a replica-lag slider shows a stale read.

scenes.title: Tko balansira load balancer?
scenes.concept: Callout: the LB is itself a SPOF: HA pair with a floating IP (VRRP), DNS with several records (slow failover), anycast, managed cloud LBs.
scenes.visual: Small figure: two LBs; the floating VIP moves on failure.

flagshipSimulation.name: Ugasite poslužitelj usred ručka
flagshipSimulation.description: The L04 rack with active/passive health checks, LB retry, per-server failure buttons and 20 users with carts. Zadaci: „Preživite pad procesa na S3 pri λ = 15 uz < 2 % grešaka”, „Ispraznite S2 bez ijedne neuspjele narudžbe”, „Nula izgubljenih sesija nakon pada bilo kojeg poslužitelja”. Incident card: λ 15, Najmanje veza, crash S3, seed 42.
controls: Klizači provjere: interval (1–10 s sim), prag neuspjeha (1–5)
Gumbi za kvar: „Ugasi Redis”, „Ugasi load balancer”
flagshipSimulation.model: sim-models SIM 1 lifecycle. Active check per server every 2 s sim (staggered), timeout 1 s; pass iff process Up; Unhealthy after 2 fails, Healthy after 2 passes; restarted servers start Unhealthy. Process crashed → port closed, routed requests get 502 at once. Machine off → no RST: new connections wait the LB connect timeout (1 s sim; badge 'NGINX proxy_connect_timeout zadano 60 s') then 502, in-flight requests hang until the 5 s client timeout → 504, probes time out. Hung → park until 5 s client timeout → 504, probes time out. Draining → no new routing, show „sigurno za uklanjanje” when inflight+queue = 0. Crashed → 6 s → Starting (3 s warm-up, probes fail) → Up. Passive: any 502/504 → eject 10 s (NGINX max_fails=1, fail_timeout=10s). LB retry: on 502 before processing, retry once elsewhere. No healthy target → 503 (toggle fail-open = ALB behaviour). Sessions: 20 users, random user per request; local store dies with its server; no affinity + local → „sesija izgubljena”; cookie affinity set on first request, reassigned if unhealthy; Redis → no loss, but Redis down → every session read fails. Validated: process crash on S3 at λ15 → RR 11, LC 37 failures in the detection window; afterwards cluster at 100 % of remaining capacity.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: „Sruši proces” under least connections shows the black hole; „Ugasi stroj” and „Zamrzni” fill queues with hollow 504s; „Ugasi Redis” logs everyone out at once – shared state is the new SPOF; „Ugasi load balancer” takes everything down.
flagshipSimulation.insight: Failure detection always has a window; a crashed process, a dead machine, a hang and a drain look different; redundancy needs spare capacity; stateless servers are interchangeable, but state moves into the database, which becomes the hard part.

codeArtifacts.title: nginx: max_fails, fail_timeout, proxy_next_upstream
codeArtifacts.purpose: Passive checks and retry; note active checks need NGINX Plus, HAProxy, Envoy or a cloud LB

codeArtifacts.title: Sesije u Redisu
codeArtifacts.purpose: Django settings: default DB sessions → SESSION_ENGINE cache + django.core.cache.backends.redis.RedisCache

misconceptions: „Load balancer odmah zna da je poslužitelj pao” — only after U consecutive failed checks: (U−1)·interval to U·interval, plus the timeout when the server hangs.
„Load balancer uklanja jedinstvenu točku kvara” — it is one unless it is redundant itself.
„Ljepljive sesije rješavaju stanje” — they skew load, lose sessions on crash and don't rebalance on scale-out; move state to Redis/DB.
„Bez stanja znači da aplikacija nema podataka” — the state lives elsewhere (Redis, DB).
„Replike za čitanje skaliraju i pisanje” — every write still goes to the primary; replicas lag and can return stale reads (DeepDive).
„CAP: uvijek birate dva od tri” — the trade-off applies only during a partition (DeepDive).
keyFacts: [sim-models] AWS ALB health checks: 30 s interval, 5 s timeout, healthy 5, unhealthy 2 → detection ≈30–60 s (≈65 s hung), re-entry ≈150 s; deregistration delay 300 s; fails open when all targets unhealthy.
[sim-models] NGINX passive: max_fails=1, fail_timeout=10s; proxy_connect_timeout default 60 s.
analogies: Vlastiti bicikl i gradski romobili: a broken scooter is swapped, not repaired. Breaks down: databases and other stateful systems keep identity (L19).
lectures.bridgeToNext: Poslužitelji aplikacije sada su zamjenjivi, a stanje živi u Postgresu i Redisu. No API sve radi sinkrono: spremi narudžbu, ispiše listić za kuhinju i pošalje SMS. U 12:00 SMS-gateway počne kasniti – i s njim zapinju sve narudžbe.

lectures.title: Redovi poruka i događaji
lectures.subtitle: Kako preživjeti nalet bez izgubljenih narudžbi – i zašto se ista narudžba ponekad skuha dvaput.
lectures.hook: SMS-gateway odgovara sve sporije, a API čeka svaki SMS, pa zapinju i narudžbe. Na Ćevap-petak narudžbe deset sekundi stižu po 15 u sekundi (inače dvije), a API ih istodobno može obrađivati samo četiri – od 445 narudžbi tog ručka izgubi se 152. Lana doda ponovne pokušaje – i teta Mira iz kuhinje viče: „Dvaput ćevapi za istu narudžbu?!” Kako odvojiti primanje narudžbe od posla koji slijedi, a da se ništa ne izgubi ni ne udvostruči?

pokazati zašto red ne povećava kapacitet

scenes.title: Red kao amortizer
scenes.concept: Bursts absorbed; if λ > kμ persists the queue grows without bound; drain time = backlog/(kμ−λ); consumers pull work (vs LB push).
scenes.visual: Two scrubbable rates; depth chart; kitchen ticket rail with cooks taking the next ticket.

scenes.title: Potvrda i ponovna isporuka
scenes.concept: Ack before processing (crash → lost, at-most-once) vs after (crash after side effect → duplicate, at-least-once). Redelivery trigger differs by broker: RabbitMQ requeues unacked deliveries immediately when the consumer's channel/connection closes (redelivered=true), and closes a consumer that doesn't ack within consumer_timeout (default 30 min); SQS uses a visibility timeout (default 30 s) after which the message reappears.
scenes.visual: Broker toggle; two crash buttons; the message reappears (instantly on disconnect in RabbitMQ, after the timer in SQS).

scenes.title: Ključ idempotentnosti
scenes.concept: Order ID + unique constraint (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) makes database effects effectively-once when the dedup row and the effect commit in one transaction. External effects (SMS gateway, card payment) need the provider's idempotency key or must tolerate an occasional duplicate: record then send → risk of loss; send then record → risk of a duplicate. Outbox pattern in a DeepDive.
scenes.visual: Teta Mira's board stamps the duplicate „već skuhano”; a separate SMS counter can still show „SMS poslan dvaput”.

scenes.title: Otrovna poruka
scenes.concept: Full-jitter backoff random(0, min(cap, base·2ⁿ)); one sentence: retries multiply load across layers (3 × 3 × 3 = 27×). RabbitMQ nack/requeue is immediate – backoff needs a retry queue (TTL + dead-letter exchange) or the delayed-message plugin; SQS supports per-message delay. Delivery limit → DLQ; RabbitMQ quorum default delivery-limit 20; without a dead-letter exchange the message is dropped.
scenes.visual: Poison message loops through the retry lane, then moves to the DLQ lane.

scenes.title: Red, pub/sub ili log
scenes.concept: Command „Skuhaj narudžbu 42” (work queue, one consumer) vs event „NarudzbaZaprimljena” (fan-out: kitchen, SMS, analytics each get a copy). Closed DeepDive „Za znatiželjne: log i Kafka”: a log keeps messages for replay; partitions, per-key order, offsets, lag; in a classic consumer group consumers beyond the partition count sit idle; Kafka ≥4.2 share groups let more consumers than partitions share work with per-message acks and no per-key order.
scenes.visual: Topology toggle work queue / fan-out; DeepDive Stepper with partitions, offsets and lag (no consumer-group sim).

flagshipSimulation.name: Kuhinjska šina
flagshipSimulation.description: E2: producer → queue → k potrošača with visible acks, redelivery, retries and DLQ; switch between direct calls and a queue, and between RabbitMQ and SQS semantics. Zadaci: „Ćevap-petak bez izgubljene narudžbe”, „Ispraznite red u < 20 s s najmanje potrošača”, „Nula dvostrukih narudžbi kad potrošač padne nakon kuhanja (RabbitMQ) ili kad obrada traje dulje od roka za potvrdu (SQS)”, „Otrovnu poruku odvojite u DLQ”. Incident card: direct mode, nalet, k 4, seed 42, run length 150 s.
controls: Segmented način: bez reda (izravni pozivi) / s redom
Klizač „Rok za potvrdu” 1–60 s (SQS: istek vidljivosti, zadano 30 s; RabbitMQ: consumer_timeout, zadano 30 min – sažeto)
Gumbi za kvar: „SMS-gateway pao”, „Sruši potrošača prije kuhanja”, „Sruši potrošača nakon kuhanja, prije potvrde”, „Spori potrošač”, „Pošalji otrovnu poruku”
flagshipSimulation.model: sim-models SIM 2. DT 10 ms; Poisson λ 2 msg/s; burst 15/s × 10 s; k 4; service Exp mean 1000 ms; maxDeliveries 5; full jitter base 500 ms cap 30 s; manual ack after processing. Tick: (1) direct mode: free consumer starts it, else lost (503); queue mode: publish or overflow policy. (2) Redelivery – SQS mode: unacked past visibility deadline (default 30 s) → visible again (receiveCount already incremented); RabbitMQ mode: consumer crash closes its connection → its unacked deliveries requeue immediately (redelivered=true, delivery count +1); a consumer exceeding consumer_timeout (slider, compressed, badge 'stvarno: 30 min') has its channel closed and deliveries requeued. (3) success → side effect (if idempotent only for unseen IDs; SMS side effect counted separately and can still duplicate) then ack; late ack after redelivery → possible duplicate; failure → DLQ if count ≥ maxDeliveries else retry after jitter (SQS: per-message delay; RabbitMQ: via retry queue with TTL + DLX). (4) idle consumers take first visible (label 'redoslijed nije zajamčen'). Auto-ack + crash → lost. Metrics: depth, in-flight, oldest age, p50/p95 publish→ack, retries, DLQ, side effects unique vs total, „SMS poslan dvaput”, lost, Little's law panel. Validated: direct 2/s, k 4 → 10,3 % lost (Erlang B 9,5 %); queue → 0 lost, p50 0,77 s, p95 3,1 s; burst direct 152/445 lost over a 150 s run; burst queue k 4 → peak ~100, drains ~50 s; k 8 → peak 66, ~15 s; pFail 10 % + poison 2 % → DLQ 24/~1245, 236 retries; SQS visibility 2 s → 13 % duplicates, 0 with idempotency. Kafka only in the DeepDive stepper: P 3, 10 user keys (hot key 50 %), partition = hash(key) mod P (text: Kafka uses murmur2), each partition to one consumer per classic group, C > P idle, lag = end − committed, commit after processing, replay resets offset.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: „SMS-gateway pao”: direct mode fails orders, queue mode keeps accepting while depth climbs then drains; crashing a consumer after cooking but before ack duplicates the order unless idempotent (and the SMS can still go out twice); in SQS mode a slow consumer past the visibility timeout duplicates too; a poison message loops until the DLQ.
flagshipSimulation.insight: A queue doesn't make work faster – it makes waiting safe; delivered twice is normal, so consumers must be idempotent – and idempotency is easy only inside your own database transaction.

misconceptions: „Red ubrzava obradu” — it absorbs bursts; if λ > kμ persists the backlog grows without bound; only more consumers add capacity.
„Svaka poruka stiže točno jednom” — at-least-once is the norm; redelivery after a crash or timeout is expected, so consumers must be idempotent.
„Poruke se obrađuju redom” — not with several consumers.
„Asinkrono znači da nitko ne čeka rezultat” — return an ID, notify later.
„Idempotentnost rješava i dvostruke SMS-ove” — only effects in the same DB transaction; external calls need the provider's idempotency key.
„Kafka treba ZooKeeper” — KRaft production-ready since 3.3; ZooKeeper removed in 4.0 (March 2025).
„Kafka ne zna raditi redove” — share groups (production-ready in 4.2) give queue-like semantics.
keyFacts: [tech-facts] At-most-once / at-least-once / exactly-once definitions; Kafka is at-least-once by default; exactly-once only within Kafka (idempotent producer + transactions + read_committed).
[tech-facts] Kafka 4.0 (2025-03-18) removed ZooKeeper; Kafka 4.2.0 (2026-02-17) share groups production-ready; current 4.3.1 (as of 2026-10).

[tech-facts] RabbitMQ 4.0 removed classic mirroring; quorum queues are the HA default, delivery-limit 20; streams are non-destructive; unacked deliveries are requeued on channel/connection close; consumer_timeout default 30 min; no per-message visibility timeout.

[tech-facts] NATS core at-most-once, JetStream at-least-once; SQS Standard at-least-once with best-effort order, visibility timeout default 30 s; SQS FIFO: strict order within a message group and send-deduplication within 5 min (AWS calls it exactly-once processing) – a message not deleted before its visibility timeout is still redelivered, so consumers stay idempotent.
analogies: Kuhinjska šina za listiće. Breaks down: paper tickets don't duplicate; real queues redeliver, so the same order can be cooked twice.
Radio emisija (pub/sub). Breaks down: late listeners miss it, but a log keeps messages for replay.

flagshipSimulation.name: Slagač stoga
flagshipSimulation.description: A 16 GB host in VM mode or container mode: add Klopa apps, watch RAM accounting, a start race and isolation. Zadaci: „Smjestite 12 aplikacija na 16 GB”, „Ograničite curenje memorije na jednu aplikaciju”, „Pronađite način u kojem napad na jezgru ne prelazi granicu”.
controls: Gumb „Dodaj aplikaciju” (api, worker, web, Postgres, Redis, RabbitMQ)
Gumbi za kvar: „Curenje memorije”, „Napad na jezgru”
flagshipSimulation.model: Host 16 GB, host OS 1 GB. VM mode: each VM reserves guest OS ~1 GB (shown as range 0,5–2 GB, 'ilustrativno') + app memory; container mode: app memory + shared runtime 0,2 GB. App memory (illustrative): api 300 MB, worker 400 MB, web 150 MB, Postgres 1 GB, Redis 200 MB, RabbitMQ 300 MB. Start race: VM stages firmware → kernel → init → app as ranges of seconds; container 'process start' as a sub-second-to-seconds range (no fake precise numbers). Leak +20 MB/s: container without memory.max → host OOM killer may kill another large process; with memory.max → only that container OOM-killed; VM mode → confined to its VM. Exploit: container mode → all containers on host (with user namespace on: still all containers, attacker labelled 'neprivilegirani korisnik na domaćinu'); VM mode → stops at hypervisor; cloud toggle → confined to one VM. The container stack never shows a guest kernel.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: „Napad na jezgru” cracks every container (user namespaces only lower the attacker's privileges) but stops at the hypervisor; „Curenje memorije” without memory.max lets the host OOM killer hit a neighbour.
flagshipSimulation.insight: A container is an isolated process sharing the host kernel – isolation is traded for density and speed; in the cloud the answer is usually both.

misconceptions: „Kontejner je lagani virtualni stroj” — an isolated host process with no kernel of its own (visible in the host's ps, same uname -r).
„Kontejneri izoliraju jednako kao VM-ovi” — they share the host kernel; a kernel exploit crosses containers, a VM stops at the hypervisor.
„Kontejneri su zamijenili VM-ove” — cloud nodes are usually VMs running containers.
„Docker na Macu radi nativno” — Docker Desktop runs Linux containers in a hidden Linux VM.
„Svaka slika radi svugdje” — CPU architecture and kernel matter (amd64 vs arm64, emulation).
keyFacts: [tech-facts] A container is an isolated process with all the files it needs; containers share the host kernel; a VM has its own kernel.
[tech-facts] Isolation via Linux namespaces (eight types incl. time) and cgroups (OCI runtime spec).
[tech-facts] Docker Desktop on macOS runs containers in a Linux VM (Apple Virtualization framework default); amd64 images run under emulation on Apple silicon.

[tech-facts] User namespaces in Pods GA in Kubernetes 1.36 (reduce privileges after an escape, do not stop kernel exploits); kubelet fails on cgroup v1 by default since 1.35; Docker 29 deprecates and Podman 6.0 drops cgroup v1.
analogies: Kuća (VM) i stan (kontejner). Breaks down: apartment walls are solid but container isolation is weaker, a container has no own kernel, and containers are disposable.
Naočale (imenski prostori) i pojas (kontrolne grupe). Breaks down: glasses and belt are added by the kernel, not worn by the process – it can't take them off.

flagshipSimulation.name: Laboratorij predmemorije izgradnje
flagshipSimulation.description: E4 on klopa-web (TypeScript, npm, Vite): Dockerfile as draggable cards; the build animates a layer stack with CACHED/REBUILT, size, short digest and a stopwatch; then push and tag panels. A second tab shows the klopa-api Dockerfile (pip). Zadaci: „Ponovna izgradnja nakon promjene koda < 5 s”, „Slika < 200 MB”, „Pronađite ključ u slici”, „Slika radi kao korisnik koji nije root”.

Gumb za kvar „Kopiraj .env pa ga obriši”
Gumbi „Pošalji u registar” i „Pomakni latest na novu sliku”
flagshipSimulation.model: Deterministic. A layer is CACHED iff its instruction and inputs are unchanged (COPY: hash of matching build-context files; RUN: parent layer + command) AND every preceding instruction (all layers beneath it in the stack) is CACHED. 'Promijeni kod' changes src (affects COPY . .); 'Promijeni ovisnosti' changes package files (COPY package*.json and COPY . .). Illustrative timings (labelled): base pull 8 s first time, npm ci 40 s, npm run build 3 s (Vite), COPY ~1 s; sizes: full node base ~1,1 GB vs slim ~250 MB, node_modules 180 MB, dev deps 120 MB, nginx-unprivileged runtime + dist ~50 MB. .dockerignore off → context includes node_modules, .git and the repo-root .env (+400 MB, COPY . . invalidated by any git change). Multi-stage → final = nginx runtime + dist only (unprivileged image listens on 8080 as a non-root user). .env trick → lower layer contains the file, whiteout above; inspector and image history reveal it. Registry stores layer digests; push uploads only missing ('Layer already exists'). Tag map tag → digest; re-pointing latest makes two nodes report different digests. Expected: COPY . . before npm ci → code edit ≈44 s; correct order ≈4 s (COPY 1 s + build 3 s). klopa-api tab: python slim base, COPY requirements.txt → pip install (≈30 s, illustrative) → COPY . . → USER → gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:8000; correct order rebuild ≈1 s.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: COPY . . before RUN npm ci re-runs the 40 s install on every code edit; „Kopiraj .env pa ga obriši” leaves the key findable; moving latest leaves two servers running different code under one name.
flagshipSimulation.insight: Order instructions from least to most frequently changing; layers are immutable, so a deleted file is only hidden; a tag is a label, a digest is the identity.

flagshipSimulation.description: A canvas of one host with web, api, worker, postgres, redis and rabbitmq; networks as regions, volumes as cylinders, published ports as doors; live compose.yaml with two-way highlight; a test browser on localhost:8080. flagshipSimulation.model: Deterministic state machine. up: create project network (user-defined bridge, embedded DNS) → named volumes → containers in depends_on order; with service_healthy a dependent waits for the dependency's healthcheck (Postgres healthy after 5 s sim); without it api starts early, fails its first DB connect and restarts if a restart policy is set. Name resolution only between services sharing a user-defined network. Host browser reaches only published ports; container localhost = itself; app bound to 127.0.0.1 inside → connection reset through the published port. Duplicate host port → 'port is already allocated'. Postgres rows: named volume mounted at /var/lib/postgresql (postgres:18+) → survive down; mount at the old /var/lib/postgresql/data path → data actually lands in the image's anonymous VOLUME; no named volume → anonymous volume: survives container restart, but docker rm db or down+up gets a fresh anonymous volume (rows 'lost', old volume dangling); down removes containers and network, keeps named volumes; down -v removes named and anonymous volumes. restart: unless-stopped → crashed container restarts with backoff; 'Ugasi računalo' → everything stops, nothing moves elsewhere.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: Moving db to another network breaks name resolution; two services on host 8080 fail; docker rm db without a named volume loses all orders (they sit in a dangling anonymous volume); „Ugasi računalo” takes all of Klopa down and no restart policy helps.
flagshipSimulation.insight: Compose already teaches declarative YAML and DNS by service name – what's missing is more than one machine and someone who keeps watch.

misconceptions: „Kontejneri razgovaraju preko IP adresa koje moram potražiti” — on a user-defined network services resolve each other by name.
„localhost u kontejneru je moje računalo” — each container has its own network namespace; localhost is the container itself.
„depends_on čeka da baza bude spremna” — only with condition: service_healthy and a healthcheck.
„Bez volumena podatci baze žive u kontejneru” — the postgres image's VOLUME creates an anonymous volume, which a recreated container doesn't reuse.
„Treba docker-compose i version: '3.8'” — v1 has been dead since July 2023; use docker compose; the version key is ignored.
„restart: always znači visoku dostupnost” — it restarts containers on the same host only; a dead host moves nothing.

[explainers] The default bridge network has no name-based DNS; user-defined networks (which Compose creates) do.
[tech-facts] postgres:18+ image: PGDATA /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker, VOLUME /var/lib/postgresql; older images used /var/lib/postgresql/data.

flagshipSimulation.name: Vi ste orkestrator → termostat za aplikacije
flagshipSimulation.description: E3: the same seeded day twice – first manually, then with „Predaj Kubernetesu”, where a generic loop fills dashed ghosts with solid instances. Scores: minutes of missing capacity, wrong placements, „Davorovi sati sna”. Zadaci: „Preživite 03:00 i 12:00 ručno”, „Isto s petljom – usporedite”, „Promijenite želju usred popravka”.

flagshipSimulation.model: 3 servers × 14 abstract slots (42; no requests yet). Baseline api 9, worker 12, web 6 = 27 containers (9 per server). Seeded events: 03:00 server-2 fails → 28 slots for 27 (fits, one spare – callback to N+1 from L05); 08:00 Davor brings server-2 back repaired – existing containers are NOT moved back (Kubernetes does not rebalance running workloads); 10:00 api replaced by a new version; 12:00 api desired 9→15 for 1 h – new instances land mostly on server-2 (most free slots). Manual: each missing desired instance costs one instance-minute. Loop: every tick (10 s sim, labelled 'stvarno: sekunde') diff = desired − actual per app; create dashed ghosts; place each on the server with most free slots (seeded tie-break); solid after 5 s; surplus removed newest first. 'Izgubi događaj' drops the notification but the next tick still sees the diff. Desired change mid-repair → converges to the latest. Desired > capacity → ghosts stay unplaced ('nema mjesta'). No component names yet.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: Server dies at 03:00: manual capacity is missing until a human notices, the loop restores it within a few ticks; a lost event changes nothing; asking for more than fits leaves ghosts waiting; a repaired server stays nearly empty until new work arrives.
flagshipSimulation.insight: You declare what, not how; independent loops compare desired with actual forever, so failures and changes are handled the same way.

flagshipSimulation.description: E3: control-plane hexagons and 3 worker nodes with watch lines; scrub replicas, apply manifests, switch components off; numbered messages and an event log like kubectl get events. Zadaci: „Povežite pet simptoma s komponentom”, „Dovedite Pod iz ImagePullBackOff do Running”.
controls: Klizač „replicas (ReplicaSet – više u L13)” 0–9 / gumb „kubectl apply”
Prekidači: API poslužitelj, etcd, raspoređivač, controller-manager, kubelet na čvoru-2
Gumbi za kvar: „Krivi tag slike”, „Napuni čvorove”, „Obriši Pod”, „Ugasi čvor”
flagshipSimulation.model: Tick 100 ms. Objects live in 'etcd'; API server is the only writer; watchers react after 100–300 ms. The replicas slider drives an object labelled 'ReplicaSet (pretpregled – detaljno u 13. predavanju)' whose controller creates/deletes Pod objects to match; the scene also contains one bare Pod (klopa-worker) that is NOT replaced when deleted, even with the controller-manager on (plants L12). Scheduler binds unbound Pods to Ready nodes with free abstract slots (requests come in L17), most free first. kubelet: pull (1 s cached / 3 s) → ContainerCreating → Running; wrong tag → ErrImagePull → ImagePullBackOff with growing retry. Off-switches: API server → kubectl errors, nothing changes, Pods keep serving; etcd → writes fail, Pods keep serving; scheduler → new Pods Pending forever; controller-manager → deleted Pod not replaced. kubelet on node-2 off → containers there keep running, node shows NotReady (Unknown) after tens of seconds (compressed); after the default 300 s not-ready toleration (badge 'stvarno ~5 min') its Pods are marked for deletion but stay Terminating because no kubelet confirms; ReplicaSet-owned Pods are recreated elsewhere, the bare Pod is not (StatefulSet Pods behave differently – L19). 'Ugasi čvor' (separate button) → machine and containers gone, same control-plane sequence. 'Napuni čvorove' → FailedScheduling '0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient memory' (mechanism in L17). Events: Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created, Started, FailedScheduling, BackOff.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: Scheduler off → Pending forever; controller-manager off → a deleted Pod is not replaced; whole control plane off → Pods keep serving but nothing heals; wrong tag → ImagePullBackOff; kubelet off → NotReady, and only after ~5 min are ReplicaSet Pods recreated elsewhere while the old ones hang in Terminating.
flagshipSimulation.insight: kubectl apply only writes onto the whiteboard; independent components watch it and work asynchronously; the data plane survives a control-plane outage.

Zadaci: „Spori start (40 s) do Ready bez ubijanja”, „Zaglavljeni proces neka se sam oporavi”, „Ispad baze od 60 s bez ijednog restarta i bez 0 endpointa”, „Dijagnosticirajte tri Poda iz stupca STATUS”.

Po provjeri (startup, liveness, readiness): uključi, endpoint /healthz (samo proces) ili /ready (zagrijan, bez baze) ili /ready-db (provjerava bazu), initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, failureThreshold
Segmented slika: dobar tag / krivi tag
Gumbi za kvar: „Zaglavi proces”, „Baza pala 60 s”, „Obriši Pod”, „Ugasi čvor”
flagshipSimulation.model: Real defaults: periodSeconds 10, timeoutSeconds 1, successThreshold 1, failureThreshold 3, initialDelaySeconds 0 (sim may compress ×5 with badge). Startup: until success liveness/readiness don't run; failureThreshold fails → kill, restartPolicy applies. Liveness fails ×threshold → container restarted (count +1, same name/IP). Readiness fail → Ready=False → no traffic, no restart. No readiness probe → Ready as soon as container starts (warm-up errors). Back-off 10, 20, 40 … 300 s, reset after 10 min clean. Wrong tag → phase Pending, STATUS ImagePullBackOff; crash at start → phase Running, STATUS CrashLoopBackOff. Behaviours: slow start → /healthz and /ready fail 40 s; deadlock → alive process, endpoints time out; /ready-db returns 503 while DB down, /healthz and /ready stay OK while the app itself answers 503 on order requests; crash at start → exit 1 after 2 s. DB 60 s outage: liveness on /ready-db → all three Pods restart after ~30 s and keep failing until DB returns; readiness on /ready-db → all NotReady → 0 targets, clients see connection errors (anti-pattern); liveness /healthz + readiness /ready → no restarts, Pods stay Ready and answer 503 quickly, recovery is instant. Bare Pods: deleted, or node off longer than the 300 s toleration → never recreated. Traffic 20 rps evenly over Ready Pods.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: Liveness on /ready-db + „Baza pala 60 s” restarts all Pods at once; readiness on /ready-db empties the traffic target list; slow start with aggressive liveness and no startup probe → CrashLoopBackOff; no readiness probe sends traffic to warming Pods; a deleted bare Pod is gone forever.
flagshipSimulation.insight: A dead process restarts itself; a stuck one needs a question – and the wrong question turns a blip into an outage; Pods are replaced, never repaired, so something must recreate them.

codeArtifacts.purpose: Liveness: only 'is this process alive' (no dependencies). Readiness: 'can this Pod serve right now' (warm-up, own state, load shedding). Do not fail readiness on a shared dependency such as the DB; stay Ready and return 503 or a degraded response.

misconceptions: „Pod je kontejner” — one or more containers sharing an IP and volumes.
„Pod se popravi na mjestu i zadrži IP” — containers restart in place, but a replacement Pod has a new name and IP.
„Web i bazu stavimo u isti Pod” — they would scale and be replaced together.
„Provjera živosti treba provjeravati bazu” — a DB blip then restarts every Pod at once.
„Provjera spremnosti neka provjerava bazu” — a shared outage makes every Pod NotReady at once and leaves 0 endpoints; answer 503 instead.
„Neuspjela provjera spremnosti restarta Pod” — it only removes the Pod from traffic.
„Bez provjera Kubernetes zna kad je aplikacija spremna” — without a readiness probe a Pod is Ready as soon as its container starts.
„STATUS je faza Poda” — STATUS shows a reason (ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff) while the phase may be Pending or Running.
„Sidecar je samo još jedan kontejner u containers” — native sidecars are initContainers with restartPolicy: Always (GA 1.33; DeepDive).
keyFacts: [tech-facts] Liveness failure restarts the container; readiness failure removes the Pod from Service traffic without restart; startup probe disables the others until it succeeds.
[tech-facts] Pod phases: Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed (Unknown); ImagePullBackOff and ContainerCreating occur in phase Pending; Ready is a Pod condition.
[tech-facts] Probe success: httpGet 200–399, exec exit 0, grpc SERVING, tcpSocket connect.
[tech-facts] Native sidecars (initContainers with restartPolicy: Always) GA in 1.33; they don't block Job completion.
[sim-models] CrashLoopBackOff 10 s, 20 s, 40 s … capped at 300 s, reset after 10 min; probe defaults 10 s / 1 s / 1 / 3 / 0; terminationGracePeriodSeconds 30.
analogies: Pod kao stan s cimerima (zajednička adresa i hladnjak). Breaks down: Pods are not long-lived homes; they are replaced, not repaired.
lectures.bridgeToNext: Noćas je čvor-2 bio nedostupan dulje od pet minuta. Kubernetes je Podove s njega izbacio, a goli Pod s API-jem nitko nije ponovno stvorio. A Petra javlja: „Vegetarijanski meni mora biti vani danas u 11:00 – bez gašenja stranice.”

flagshipSimulation.name: Kontrolna ploča uvođenja
flagshipSimulation.description: E3: Deployment klopa-api with ReplicaSet tree, revision history, invariant gauges and 20 rps of traffic coloured by version (1.3.2 blue, 1.4.0 violet, 1.5.0 rose). Zadaci: „Uvedite 1.4.0 bez ijednog neuspjelog zahtjeva”, „Nikad ispod 4 dostupna Poda”, „Oporavite se od 1.5.0 u < 30 s sim vremena”.
controls: maxSurge i maxUnavailable: 0, 1, 2, 25 %, 50 %, 100 % (poruka kad su oba 0)
flagshipSimulation.model: sim-models SIM 5 (rolling.go). DT 100 ms. surge = ceil(maxSurge%·N), unavail = floor(maxUnavailable%·N); both 0 after rounding → unavail 1; explicit 0/0 rejected ('maxSurge i maxUnavailable ne mogu oba biti 0'). Each reconcile scales up OR down: maxTotal = N + surge; all = Σ rs.spec.replicas (terminating NOT counted); if all < maxTotal → newRS += min(maxTotal − all, N − newRS); else minAvailable = N − unavail; maxScaledDown = all − minAvailable − (newRS.spec − newRS.available); ≤0 → stop; clean up unhealthy old first, then scale old (oldest first) down by Σavailable − minAvailable. Available = Ready ≥ minReadySeconds (0); traffic follows Ready. Recreate: old → 0, wait until gone, then new. Timings (sim): schedule 1 s, pull 4 s new (0 cached), start 6 s, readiness period 2 s in YAML (real default 10), progressDeadlineSeconds 60 in YAML (real 600), shutdown 2 s. No readiness probe → Ready on start → errors during 6 s warm-up. Validated N=4: 25/25 28 s, peak incl. terminating 7, min available 3; 1/0 51 s, peak 6, min 4; 0/1 46 s, peak 5, min 3; 100 %/0 17 s, peak 8. Crashing image stalls at 3 old + 2 new; N=10 surge 3 unavail 2 stalls at 8 old / 5 new (matches docs). Show .status.terminatingReplicas. Undo = scale previous RS up by the same rules; history shows kubernetes.io/change-cause. Deleting the Deployment cascades.
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: Pushing the crashing 1.5.0 stalls at 3 old + 2 new (75 % capacity) and shows ProgressDeadlineExceeded – nothing rolls back by itself; Recreate empties the app during lunch; readiness off shows errors from warming Pods.
flagshipSimulation.insight: A rollout is two ReplicaSets scaled in opposite directions under two limits; readiness is the gatekeeper; rollback is scaling the old ReplicaSet up – and someone must ask for it.

misconceptions: „Deployment i postavljanje su isto” — object vs act.
„Više replika znači više računala” — replicas are Pods; many can share a node, and full nodes leave them Pending.
„Postupno ažuriranje je uvijek bez prekida” — needs readiness and compatible versions.
„Deployment se sam vraća na staru verziju” — the rollout stalls with ProgressDeadlineExceeded; rollback is rollout undo or tooling.
„Deployment izravno upravlja Podovima” — through ReplicaSets, which hold the revision history.
„minReadySeconds odgađa promet” — traffic follows Ready; it only delays 'Available'.
„Blue-green i canary ugrađeni su u Deployment” — only RollingUpdate and Recreate.
keyFacts: [tech-facts] Deployment → ReplicaSet → Pods; strategies RollingUpdate (default maxSurge 25 %, maxUnavailable 25 %) and Recreate; revisionHistoryLimit 10; progressDeadlineSeconds 600; roll back with kubectl rollout undo.
[tech-facts] 'Deployment' has two meanings (act and object); Kubernetes does not deploy source code.
[sim-models] maxSurge rounds up, maxUnavailable down; terminating Pods not counted (status.terminatingReplicas beta since 1.35).
[tech-facts] kubectl --record is deprecated; use the kubernetes.io/change-cause annotation.
analogies: Ugovor o smjeni: „uvijek četiri konobara, zamijeni svakoga tko ode, uniforme mijenjaj jednog po jednog”. Breaks down: the contract doesn't name the waiter – Pods must be interchangeable.
lectures.bridgeToNext: Vegetarijanski meni je vani. Ali novi Podovi imaju nove IP adrese, a klopa-web je imao upisanu adresu jednog API Poda – i sada vraća greške. Kako drugi pronalaze Podove koji stalno mijenjaju adresu?

scenes.title: Oznake i selektor
scenes.concept: Pod IPs are temporary; Service selects Pods (not Deployments) by labels in its own Namespace; typo app: klopa-apii → 0 endpoints.
scenes.visual: Label stickers; endpoint lines attach/detach.

scenes.title: Samo spremni
scenes.concept: EndpointSlices list every matching Pod with conditions ready, serving and terminating; kube-proxy sends traffic only to ready ones. A readiness failure flips ready: false without restart; replay the L13 rollout with readiness → 0 errors; EndpointSlices replace the deprecated Endpoints API.
scenes.visual: Ready endpoints as solid lines, not-ready as dashed lines carrying no traffic; replayed rollout.

scenes.visual: Name assembled piece by piece.

scenes.title: Put paketa
scenes.concept: ClusterIP is virtual; kube-proxy rules on the client's own node DNAT to a random ready Pod; conntrack rewrites the reply; iptables default in 1.37, nftables successor, ipvs deprecated; eBPF dataplanes one line.
scenes.visual: Packet header labels rewriting in place.

scenes.title: Service nije klasični load balancer
scenes.concept: L04 rack in Service mode: random per connection, no weights, ignores node size (uneven capacity is handled by requests/scheduler L17 and HPA L18); long-lived keep-alive/HTTP/2/gRPC connections pin to one Pod; fixes: new connections, an L7 proxy (the Gateway balances per request, L15), client-side balancing over a headless Service (L19). sessionAffinity: ClientIP (10800 s) is IP-based, not cookie-based: everyone behind campus NAT or eduroam shares one public IP and lands on the same Pod, and behind a cloud LB the Pod may see only the LB's or node's address unless externalTrafficPolicy: Local is set; cookie affinity lives at L7.
scenes.visual: Per-Pod hit histogram for each client mode; affinity toggle collapsing a whole campus onto one Pod.

scenes.title: Vrste i tiho gašenje
scenes.concept: ClusterIP (default) → LoadBalancer (cloud or add-on; stays pending on kind unless cloud-provider-kind runs); NodePort 30000–32767 in one line; endpoint removal is async with SIGTERM → preStop sleep, grace 30 s.
scenes.visual: Reachability rings; shutdown race timeline.

flagshipSimulation.name: Laboratorij selektora i put paketa
flagshipSimulation.description: E3 + E1 Service mode: Pods with draggable labels, selector chips and live EndpointSlice lines; per-Pod readiness; a client Pod with a hit histogram; rollout replay; the L04 rack reopened in Service mode. Zadaci: „Popravite Service bez endpointa”, „Uvođenje 1.4.0 → 1.4.1 s 0 grešaka”, „Rasporedite keep-alive klijenta na sva 4 Poda”, „Objasnite zašto svaki Pod dobiva jednako prometa bez obzira na veličinu čvora – i kako veći čvor ipak dobije više prometa (na njega stane više Podova, L17)”.
controls: Segmented klijent: nova veza po zahtjevu / jedna dugotrajna veza / N veza
Gumbi za kvar: „Greška u selektoru”, „Podu padne readiness”, „Upiši IP pa uvedi novu verziju”
flagshipSimulation.model: EndpointSlice = Pods in the namespace matching ALL selector pairs, each with conditions ready/serving/terminating; kube-proxy routes only to ready endpoints (not-ready drawn dashed, terminating marked); recomputed on change, propagated to every node's rules after 1 s (sim). Each NEW connection picks a ready backend uniformly at random (iptables/nftables default); all requests on it go to that Pod; sessionAffinity ClientIP pins by source IP for 10800 s (a NAT'd campus = one IP = one Pod). No weights, node size ignored. 0 ready endpoints → requests fail. Client modes: per-request connections → random spread with visible variance; one keep-alive connection → 100 % on one Pod; N connections → N random picks. Shutdown: deletion sends SIGTERM and starts endpoint removal concurrently; app exiting immediately drops requests arriving in the 1 s lag; preStop sleep 5 → 0 drops; SIGKILL after 30 s. Packet stepper: 10.244.1.7 → DNS → 10.96.12.7:80 → DNAT 10.244.2.15:8000 → reply via conntrack. Service mode of the L04 engine behaves like random (≈RR: λ15 → ~2,7 % errors on the default rack).
flagshipSimulation.breakIt: A selector typo leaves 0 endpoints while all Pods are healthy; one keep-alive connection sends 100 % to one Pod; ClientIP affinity behind NAT sends a whole campus to one Pod; a hardcoded IP breaks on the next rollout; without preStop a few requests fail during a rollout.
flagshipSimulation.insight: A Service is a stable name and virtual IP implemented as rules on every node; it selects by labels, sends only to ready endpoints and balances connections at random, not requests in turn.

misconceptions: „Service je proces ili kutija kroz koju prolazi promet” — a virtual IP implemented as rules on every node.
„Service raspoređuje round robin po zahtjevu” — a random backend per new connection.
„Service pokazuje na Deployment” — it selects Pods by labels; a typo gives 0 endpoints.
„EndpointSlice sadrži samo spremne Podove” — it lists not-ready ones too, with ready: false; kube-proxy skips them.
„type: LoadBalancer radi svugdje” — needs a cloud controller or add-on; stays pending on kind.
„Kratko ime radi iz svakog Namespacea” — only within the same Namespace.
„Kubernetes prati Podove iza Servicea preko objekta Endpoints” — EndpointSlices; the Endpoints API is deprecated since 1.33.
„Za performanse koristite ipvs” — deprecated since 1.35; nftables is the successor.
„gRPC se balansira po zahtjevu” — HTTP/2 keeps one long-lived connection pinned to one Pod.
keyFacts: [tech-facts] Service types ClusterIP (default), NodePort (30000–32767), LoadBalancer, ExternalName, headless (clusterIP: None, L19).
[tech-facts] kube-proxy: iptables default in 1.37; nftables GA since 1.33 (kernel ≥5.13) is the successor; ipvs deprecated since 1.35, off by default from 1.40, removal planned 1.43 (as of 2026-10).
[tech-facts] iptables/nftables pick a backend at random per connection; sessionAffinity ClientIP timeout 10800 s; trafficDistribution PreferSameZone / PreferSameNode (GA 1.35).
[tech-facts] Endpoints API deprecated in 1.33 in favour of EndpointSlices; endpoints carry ready/serving/terminating conditions; failing readiness sets ready: false.

[tech-facts] Service.spec.externalIPs deprecated in 1.36; on kind LoadBalancer stays pending unless cloud-provider-kind runs; bare-metal LoadBalancer needs an add-on such as MetalLB (mention only as example).
analogies: Glavni broj telefona tvrtke. Breaks down: there is no receptionist – only forwarding rules on every node; a ClusterIP can't usually be pinged; the pick is random per connection.
Oznake kao hashtagovi, selektor kao spremljena pretraga. Breaks down: a selector matches only Pods in the Service's own Namespace and needs ALL listed key=value pairs to match exactly.

scenes.title: Zašto ne LoadBalancer za svaki Service
scenes.concept: Cost and certificate sprawl; cloud L4 LB → L7 Gateway → Pods. The HTTPRoute names a Service, but most implementations (Envoy Gateway, Istio, NGINX Gateway Fabric, Cilium, Traefik) use it only to look up ready endpoints from its EndpointSlices and send each request straight to a Pod IP with their own L7 algorithm (round robin or least request, implementation-specific) – the L04 algorithms come back here. kube-proxy's random per-connection choice applies to in-cluster ClusterIP traffic.
scenes.visual: € counter; layered path with the ClusterIP hop drawn as bypassed.

scenes.title: Dodatak, a ne ugrađeni dio
